title: Avlat
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: A great sage among the nations, Shmuel’s friend and companion. Avodah Zarah 30a relates that they sat together when cooked wine was brought. Avlat drew back his hand to avoid touching it, but Shmuel told him that cooked wine was not subject to the prohibition of libation wine. In Shabbat 129a Avlat calls Shmuel “the sage of the Jews.” In 156b, as they sat watching men go to the marsh, Avlat said: “That man will not return: a snake will bite and kill him.” Shmuel replied, “If he is an Israelite, he will go and return,” and so he did. In Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat, chapter 3, end of halakhah 3, and Beitzah 2:5, Avlat questions Levi the eunuch; Hyman says that without doubt it should read Levi bar Sisi.

notes.text: Hyman calls Avlat a sage of the nations, not a Babylonian Amora. Levi the eunuch becoming Levi bar Sisi is Hyman’s proposed correction; it is not silently adopted in a source.

The consulted Shabbat 156b continues the marsh episode with the snake and the man’s charity. Jerusalem Talmud Beitzah 2:5 directly has Avlat questioning Levi Sarisa and a eunuch analogy in the answer. Hyman’s confident proposed Levi bar Sisi correction remains his, without silently changing that received name or admitting a sage identity.
